# 3ngram v1.8.0

Minor: the revise tool stops re-filing memories by accident and learns to
refile them on purpose, `get_memories` points a superseded row at its
successor, and the v1.7.0 train (session-run read endpoints, a consolidation
queue that settles, overdue commitments that stay visible) ships with it.

v1.7.0 was versioned on staging but never tagged: three more changes landed
before the promotion, so this release carries the whole train since v1.6.3.

## Changes

- **`revise` inherits filing from the predecessor** (#222, #238). The revise
  schema extended the remember schema and so inherited its literal defaults:
  a revise that left out `scope` wrote the successor as `personal`, with no
  project and no tags, while closing the original. `scope`, `project` and
  `tags` are now optional with no default on revise; an omitted value is
  copied from the predecessor inside the revise transaction, and both
  transports echo the filing the successor was written with. Explicit values
  still override; a project can be replaced but not cleared.

- **`revise` move disposition** (#233, #241). `{ kind: "move", predecessorId,
  scope?, project?, tags? }` changes a memory's filing in place: no successor,
  no edge, content, topic, status and the bi-temporal columns untouched, so a
  refile neither floods the target project's recent section nor breaks
  `asOf` reads. Audited by a `revise` memory event recording scope, project
  and tag count before and after. Works on superseded and archived rows. The
  move takes the account-lifecycle guard first and the row lock after
  provenance; a no-op move writes nothing and attaches no session. Hard rule
  1 in AGENTS.md gains this single carve-out. The object schema exports keep
  their shapes; the successor-or-move union is new under
  `reviseRequestSchema` / `nativeReviseRequestSchema` /
  `reviseToolRequestSchema`.

- **`get_memories` returns `supersededBy`** (#223, #239). Each item names
  its direct successor (`{ id, edgeType }`) when the row is superseded, or
  `null`. Superseded follows REST history's precedence: not archived, closed
  validity, and a `supersedes`/`updates` edge; for active rows that matches
  `search`'s `superseded` flag. One hop only; lineage stays with REST
  history.

- **Read endpoints for agent-session rows and triage attempts** (#203, #215).
  `GET /api/v1/agent-sessions/{sessionRunId}` and
  `.../triage-attempts`, read-only and tenant-scoped, backed by migration
  `0037_triage_attempt_log`.

- **Consolidation no longer re-proposes a settled pair** (#220, #231). A pair
  with a proposal in any status, or with a materialized edge, in either
  orientation, is excluded at candidate time. Production logs had shown the
  same 218 candidate pairs and zero new proposals on 121 consecutive runs.

- **Overdue commitments stay open for a grace window** (#221, #232).
  `COMMITMENT_EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS` (default 14; `0` restores immediate expiry;
  blank counts as unset) keeps a past-due commitment open, and therefore
  overdue in the briefing, before the worker expires it. Library callers of
  `surface()` and `sweepCommitments()` that omit the new optional argument
  keep the previous semantics.

## Known gap

The `revise` tool's one-line description still reads "never edits in place";
the move kind makes that inaccurate. Refreshing it requires regenerating the
tool-selection embeddings, which needs an OpenAI key; a description-refresh
covering #222, #223 and #233 follows in a later release. The field
descriptions and the concept docs carry the current semantics.

## Operations

One migration: `0037_triage_attempt_log` (schema head 0036 to 0037). Run it
before the server promote, as the deploy runbook requires. The worker gains
one optional environment variable, `COMMITMENT_EXPIRY_GRACE_DAYS`; both
Compose stacks pass it through. Both triage mechanisms
(`SESSION_CLOSER_ENABLED`, `THREENGRAM_STOP_NUDGE`) remain **default-off**
pending the #166 validation bar.
